theme: 3 terms on small building blocks: a range of values, a group of values and a new name for a type

terms.definition: A value that covers everything from a start to an end, written like `1...5`.
terms.example: Loop over a range from 1 to 5, and use each number once.

terms.definition: A value that groups several values together, and each part can have its own label.
terms.example: Return a tuple with the `name` and the `age`, so both travel together.

terms.definition: A way to give an existing type a new, clearer name.
terms.example: Add a typealias called `UserID`, so the code reads more clearly.
terms.code:
typealias UserID = Int
let id: UserID = 42
print(id)

video.description:
Learn to talk about small building blocks in Swift: Range, Tuple & Typealias, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Range - A value that covers everything from a start to an end, written like `1...5`.
Tuple - A value that groups several values together, and each part can have its own label.
Typealias - A way to give an existing type a new, clearer name.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Range, Tuple & Typealias in English | Day 20
landscape.description:
Explain Range, Tuple & Typealias in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Range, 튜플, 타입별칭 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Range - A value that covers everything from a start to an end, written like `1...5`.
한국어: 레인지: `1...5`처럼 시작부터 끝까지의 값을 나타내는 값

Tuple - A value that groups several values together, and each part can have its own label.
한국어: 튜플: 여러 값을 하나로 묶는 값, 각 부분에 이름을 붙일 수 있음

Typealias - A way to give an existing type a new, clearer name.
한국어: 타입별칭: 이미 있는 타입에 더 알기 쉬운 새 이름을 붙이는 방법

In this video, Mina and Jake write a score value with levels, labels and a clearer type name, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

dialogue.title: Levels and scores

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, I need levels 1 to 3. How do I write that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use a Range. Write `1...3`, like `let levels = 1...3`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So a Range covers every number from the start to the end?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Now I want to return a name and a score together.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use a Tuple. Write `(name: String, score: Score)`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wait, what is `Score`? I only see `Int` in Swift.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good catch. It is a Typealias: `typealias Score = Int`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So a Typealias only gives `Int` a clearer name?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Then read the Tuple part with `best.score`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. A Range, a Tuple and a Typealias make my code easier to read.

dialogue.code:
typealias Score = Int
let levels = 1...3
let best: (name: String, score: Score) = ("Mina", 90)
let top = best.score
